blocks.text: How do I find the sum of an arithmetic series?

blocks.md: - An **arithmetic series** is the sum of the terms of an **arithmetic sequence**

blocks.alt: Arithm Series Illustr, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- The following formulae will let you find the sum of the first ***n*** terms of an arithmetic series: $S_{n}=\frac{n}{2}(2a+(n-1)d)$   or   $S_{n}=\frac{n}{2}(a+l)$

  - *a *is the first term
  - *d *is the common difference
  - *l *is the last term

- You can use whichever formula is more convenient for a given question
- The ***a*** and the ***d*** in those formulae are exactly the same as the ones used with **arithmetic sequences**

blocks.text: How do I prove the arithmetic series formula?

blocks.md:
- Learn this proof of the arithmetic series formula – you can be asked to give it on the exam:

  - Write the terms out once in order
  - Write the terms out again in reverse order
  - Add the two sums together
  
    - The terms will pair up to give the same sum $2a+(n-1)d$
    - There will be *n *of these terms
  - Divide by two as two of the sums have been added together ![Arithm Series Proof, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes](assets/96bd5ab585a8-4-4-2-arithm-series-proof.png)
